terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Compile the log with javac, then run it with java Logbook.

tasks.title: Fix the name the compiler cannot find
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `Logbook.java`, the compiler refuses the line that makes `seatsLeft` with `cannot find symbol`. Fix that line so `seatsLeft` is the `seats` with the passengers who boarded taken away.

Check compiles and runs your Task 1 lines with numbers of its own and reads `seatsLeft`.
nextSteps: Run `javac Logbook.java` and find the error that names line 22.
Read the `symbol:` line under it: it names what the compiler does not know.
Compare that name with the variables made above Task 1.
Fix the name, then compile again.
hints: `cannot find symbol` means the compiler met a name nobody made. The `symbol:` line says which.
The name in the error is close to one of the variables at the top of `main`, but not the same. Every letter counts.
Change the misspelt name on that line to the variable that holds the passengers who boarded. Do not make a new variable.

tasks.title: Fix the type that does not fit
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, the compiler refuses the line that makes `code` with `incompatible types`. Fix it so `code` holds the luggage tag: the first three letters of `destination`, in capitals, as the line already works out.

Check compiles and runs your Task 2 lines with destinations of its own and reads `code`.
nextSteps: Find the error for line 27 and read it from the left.
It names two types: the type of the value, and the type of the variable.
Decide which of the two is wrong for a tag of three letters.
Fix that one word, then compile again.
hints: `incompatible types: A cannot be converted to B` means a value of type A is put into a variable of type B.
`substring` and `toUpperCase` give a `String`. A `char` holds exactly one character.
Change the type in front of `code`, and leave the rest of the line as it is.

tasks.title: Give the notice a value every time
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, once Tasks 1 and 2 compile, javac refuses the line that prints `notice` with `variable notice might not have been initialized`. Fix it so `notice` says `No crossings today` when `windKnots` is 30 or more, and `Boats running` otherwise.

Check compiles and runs your Task 3 lines with winds of its own, 30 knots exactly included, and reads `notice`.
nextSteps: Fix Tasks 1 and 2 and compile again: this error shows only after they are gone.
Follow the program by hand with a light wind. Which line gives `notice` a value?
Give `notice` a value on the way through where the `if` does not run.
Compile, run, and change `windKnots` at the top for a moment to see both notices.
hints: The compiler looks at every way through the code. With a light wind, the `if` is skipped.
`notice` needs a value on both ways: when the condition is true and when it is false.
Add `else { notice = "Boats running"; }` after the closing brace of the `if`.

tasks.title: Stop the crash on a day without crossings
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, the log compiles but stops with an exception when there were no crossings. Fix it so `averageLoad` is the passengers today divided by the crossings today, in whole passengers, and `0` on a day without crossings, so the log carries on to its last line.

Check runs your Task 4 lines with days of its own, one without crossings, and reads `averageLoad`.
nextSteps: Once the file compiles, run `java Logbook` and read the stack trace.
Its first line says what went wrong. The line starting with `at` says which line of `Logbook.java`.
Decide what `averageLoad` should be when `crossingsToday` is 0, and what it should be otherwise.
Make that decision with `if` and `else`, compile and run again.
hints: `ArithmeticException: / by zero` means a whole number was divided by 0. The compiler cannot see it coming, because it depends on the values.
Only divide when there was at least one crossing. A day without crossings gets 0.
The shape is `int averageLoad;` then `if (crossingsToday == 0) { averageLoad = 0; } else { averageLoad = ...; }`.
